title: Localization at a prime commutes with filtered colimits of rings
statement: Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $i\mapsto R_i$ a functor from $I$ to the category of commutative rings, with colimit $R=\varinjlim_IR_i$ in that category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\iota_i:R_i\to R$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal and put $\mathfrak p_i=\iota_i^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$, a prime ideal of $R_i$. Then: (1) for every morphism $a:i\to j$ of $I$ one has $R(a)^{-1}(\mathfrak p_j)=\mathfrak p_i$, so $R(a)$ induces a ring map $(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}\to(R_j)_{\mathfrak p_j}$, $x/s\mapsto R(a)(x)/R(a)(s)$, between the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and these maps form a functor $i\mapsto(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ from $I$ to commutative rings; (2) the ring maps $\kappa_i:(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}\to R_{\mathfrak p}$, $x/s\mapsto\iota_i(x)/\iota_i(s)$, are well defined and make $R_{\mathfrak p}$ a colimit of this functor in the category of commutative rings: $R_{\mathfrak p}=\varinjlim_I(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 037D (lemma-colimit-normal-ring), algebra.tex line 8323: 'Then we see that $R_{\mathfrak p} = \colim_i (R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$', asserted there without proof for a directed system; the description of a directed colimit of rings is Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit) and Lemma Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit); localization is Definition Tag 00CO (definition-localization)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the functor $i\mapsto(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$).* Write $D_i=(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ and $S_i=R_i\setminus\mathfrak p_i$. Each $\mathfrak p_i=\iota_i^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$ is a prime ideal of $R_i$ (the preimage of a prime ideal under a ring map: $1\notin\mathfrak p_i$ since $\iota_i(1)=1\notin\mathfrak p$, and $xy\in\mathfrak p_i$ means $\iota_i(x)\iota_i(y)\in\mathfrak p$). For $a:i\to j$ the cocone identity $\iota_j\circ R(a)=\iota_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $R(a)^{-1}(\mathfrak p_j)=R(a)^{-1}\iota_j^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=(\iota_j\circ R(a))^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p_i$, so $R(a)(S_i)\subset S_j$. Hence $D(a):D_i\to D_j$, $x/s\mapsto R(a)(x)/R(a)(s)$, is well defined [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]: $R(a)(s)\in S_j$, and if $x/s=x'/s'$ in $D_i$, i.e. $u(xs'-x's)=0$ with $u\in S_i$, then $R(a)(u)\in S_j$ and $R(a)(u)\big(R(a)(x)R(a)(s')-R(a)(x')R(a)(s)\big)=0$. It is a ring map because the sum and product of fractions are given by the formulas $x/s+x'/s'=(xs'+x's)/(ss')$, $(x/s)(x'/s')=(xx')/(ss')$, $1=1/1$, which the ring map $R(a)$ respects. From $R(\mathrm{id}_i)=\mathrm{id}$ and $R(b\circ a)=R(b)\circ R(a)$ one reads off $D(\mathrm{id}_i)=\mathrm{id}$ and $D(b\circ a)=D(b)\circ D(a)$ on every fraction $x/s$: $i\mapsto D_i$ is a functor $I\to$ commutative rings. This is part (1).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 037D (lemma-colimit-normal-ring), line 8321 ('Set $\mathfrak p_i=R_i\cap\mathfrak p$'); fractions as in Definition Tag 00CO (definition-localization), line 1068; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 2 (the cocone $\kappa_i$).* For $s\in S_i$ one has $\iota_i(s)\notin\mathfrak p$ by the definition of $\mathfrak p_i$, so $\kappa_i:D_i\to R_{\mathfrak p}$, $x/s\mapsto\iota_i(x)/\iota_i(s)$, is defined; it is well defined (if $u(xs'-x's)=0$ with $u\in S_i$, then $\iota_i(u)\notin\mathfrak p$ witnesses $\iota_i(x)/\iota_i(s)=\iota_i(x')/\iota_i(s')$) and a ring map, by the formulas for sum, product and $1$ of fractions [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], exactly as in step 1. For $a:i\to j$, $\kappa_j(D(a)(x/s))=\iota_j(R(a)(x))/\iota_j(R(a)(s))=\iota_i(x)/\iota_i(s)=\kappa_i(x/s)$ by $\iota_j\circ R(a)=\iota_i$; so $(R_{\mathfrak p},(\kappa_i))$ is a cocone on $i\mapsto D_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 037D (lemma-colimit-normal-ring), line 8322-8323 (the maps implicit in '$R_{\mathfrak p}=\colim_i(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$'); written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 3 (every element of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ comes from a stage).* Let $z\in R_{\mathfrak p}$, $z=r/\sigma$ with $r\in R$, $\sigma\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Commutative rings are the commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebras (every ring map is $\mathbf Z$-linear), so $R$ is the colimit of $i\mapsto R_i$ in commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebras, and by part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (with base ring $\mathbf Z$) $r=\iota_i(x)$, $\sigma=\iota_j(s)$ for some objects $i,j$ and $x\in R_i$, $s\in R_j$. As $I$ is filtered [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] there are $a:i\to k$, $b:j\to k$; then $r=\iota_k(x')$, $\sigma=\iota_k(s')$ with $x'=R(a)(x)$, $s'=R(b)(s)$, and $s'\in S_k$ because $\iota_k(s')=\sigma\notin\mathfrak p$. So $z=\kappa_k(x'/s')$. Combining with filteredness and the cocone identity of step 2, finitely many elements of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ are images under one $\kappa_k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit), line 778, for directed systems; here in the filtered form of the leaf; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 4 (equality criterion).* Let $w\in D_i$, $w'\in D_j$ with $\kappa_i(w)=\kappa_j(w')$. Then there are $e:i\to n$, $e':j\to n$ with $D(e)(w)=D(e')(w')$. Proof: choose $a:i\to k$, $b:j\to k$ ($I$ filtered) and replace $w,w'$ by $D(a)(w)=x/s$, $D(b)(w')=y/t$ in $D_k$ (step 2: $\kappa_k\circ D(a)=\kappa_i$). Then $\iota_k(x)/\iota_k(s)=\iota_k(y)/\iota_k(t)$ in $R_{\mathfrak p}$, so by the definition of equality of fractions [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] there is $u\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $u\,\iota_k(xt-ys)=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2) (base ring $\mathbf Z$, as in step 3) $u=\iota_l(v)$ with $v\in R_l$; choose $c:k\to m$, $d:l\to m$ and put $v'=R(d)(v)$, $q=R(c)(xt-ys)$; then $\iota_m(v'q)=u\,\iota_k(xt-ys)=0$ and $v'\in S_m$ since $\iota_m(v')=u\notin\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] there is $f:m\to n$ with $R(f)(v'q)=0$. With $g=f\circ c:k\to n$ and $v''=R(f)(v')\in S_n$ (step 1: $R(f)(S_m)\subset S_n$) this reads $v''\big(R(g)(x)R(g)(t)-R(g)(y)R(g)(s)\big)=0$, i.e. $D(g)(x/s)=D(g)(y/t)$ in $D_n$; so $e=g\circ a$, $e'=g\circ b$ work. (Conversely $D(e)(w)=D(e')(w')$ implies $\kappa_i(w)=\kappa_j(w')$ by step 2.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit), line 811, for directed systems; here in the filtered form of the leaf; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 5 (universal property).* Let $(T,(g_i:D_i\to T))$ be a cocone of commutative rings on $i\mapsto D_i$. Define $g:R_{\mathfrak p}\to T$ by $g(\kappa_i(w))=g_i(w)$: every $z\in R_{\mathfrak p}$ has the form $\kappa_i(w)$ (step 3), and if $\kappa_i(w)=\kappa_j(w')$ then with $e,e'$ from step 4, $g_i(w)=g_n(D(e)(w))=g_n(D(e')(w'))=g_j(w')$, so $g$ is well defined. It is a ring map: for $z,z'\in R_{\mathfrak p}$ choose by step 3 one $k$ and $w,w'\in D_k$ with $z=\kappa_k(w)$, $z'=\kappa_k(w')$; then $z+z'=\kappa_k(w+w')$, $zz'=\kappa_k(ww')$, so $g(z+z')=g_k(w)+g_k(w')$ and $g(zz')=g_k(w)g_k(w')$; and $g(1)=g_i(1)=1$ for any object $i$ ($I$ is nonempty, being filtered). By construction $g\circ\kappa_i=g_i$ for all $i$, and any ring map $h$ with $h\circ\kappa_i=g_i$ for all $i$ equals $g$, since the images of the $\kappa_i$ cover $R_{\mathfrak p}$ (step 3). Hence $(R_{\mathfrak p},(\kappa_i))$ is a colimit of $i\mapsto(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], which is part (2).

lean.statement: theorem filteredColimitLocalizationAtPrime {I : Type v} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{v}) [HasColimit F] (p : Ideal ((colimit F : CommRingCat) : Type v)) [hp : p.IsPrime] : let ι : ∀ i : I, (F.obj i) ⟶ colimit F := fun i => colimit.ι F i let pᵢ : ∀ i : I, Ideal ((F.obj i : CommRingCat) : Type v) := fun i => Ideal.comap (ι i).hom p (∀ i : I, (pᵢ i).IsPrime) ∧ (∀ (i j : I) (a : i ⟶ j), Ideal.comap (F.map a).hom (pᵢ j) = pᵢ i) ∧ ∃ (D : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{v}) (hD : ∀ i : I, D.obj i = CommRingCat.of (Localization.AtPrime (pᵢ i))), (∀ (i j : I) (a : i ⟶ j), CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (F.obj i) (Localization.AtPrime (pᵢ i))) ≫ eqToHom (hD i).symm ≫ D.map a = F.map a ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (F.obj j) (Localization.AtPrime (pᵢ j))) ≫ eqToHom (hD j).symm) ∧ ∃ (c : Cocone D) (hc : c.pt = CommRingCat.of (Localization.AtPrime p)), (∀ i : I, CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (F.obj i) (Localization.AtPrime (pᵢ i))) ≫ eqToHom (hD i).symm ≫ c.ι.app i ≫ eqToHom hc = ι i ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap ((colimit F : CommRingCat) : Type v) (Localization.AtPrime p))) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c)
